hints.content:
$f'(x)>0$ means $f$ is **increasing**.

$f'(x)<0$ means $f$ is **decreasing**.

$f''(x)>0$ means the slope of $f$ is increasing ($f$ is **concave up**).

$f''(x)<0$ means the slope of $f$ is decreasing ($f$ is **concave down**).

| | $f'(x)>0$ | $f'(x)<0$
:- | :- | :-: | :-:
| | $f$ is **increasing** | $f$ is **decreasing**
$f''(x)>0$ | $f$ is **concave up** |  ![A curve moves upward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/fad1dc95cd761b6e7f4c581c7093841fcf16029a) | ![A curve moves downward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/88e8d1ff71cbe909ea256814c06e1ff2df39bd5e)
$f''(x)<0$ | $f$ is **concave down** | ![A curve moves upward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/f9425dbee4d4f73f6188a62f88f637018843d7c8) | ![A curve moves downward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/4d64d76d6423a90abf605dfe2b856e7327f92a0c)

We are asked to find an interval where $f'(x)>0$ and $f''(x)>0$, so we need an interval where the graph of $f$ has this general shape:

 ![A curve moves upward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/fad1dc95cd761b6e7f4c581c7093841fcf16029a)

Visually, this is where $f'(x)>0$ and $f''(x)>0$.

![The graph of function f has a portion of the curve highlighted. The portion starts at about (negative 1, negative 50), moves upward concave up, and ends at about (2, negative 25).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/b903375c1b379c98a7985d948f20b15370b9ba91)

Now we can check each option:

Interval | Shape | Is $f'(x)>0$ and $f''(x)>0$?
:-: | :-: | :-:
$-4<x<-1$ | ![A curve moves downward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/1423ac842506af6991b8e635c34a9d36faf33368) | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f''(x)>0$ but $f'(x)<0$.
$-3<x<-2$ |![A curve moves downward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/1423ac842506af6991b8e635c34a9d36faf33368) | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f''(x)>0$ but $f'(x)<0$.
$3<x<4$ | ![A curve moves upward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/422cf5924dbecfc98054d87696663b0145ce07e6) | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f'(x)<0$ and $f''(x)<0$.
